Maria S.: Customer hit intermittent 502s while consuming SSE chat stream. They provided trace id `trace=7f9c2b1a` and timestamp 2026-03-16T14:03:12Z. Can we get a curl repro and a quick checklist of what to collect?

Raj P.: On it. First ask: are they going through a proxy or gateway? 502 + SSE usually proxy timeout or TLS munging.

Maria S.: They say app sits behind a corporate proxy and sometimes gets a 502 body mid-stream. Also reported one instance with HTTP/2 fallback.

Eli K.: Ok. Quick repro curl I usually give customers for SSE streaming (include auth + headers + raw output):

```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: customer-req-7721" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-xyz&stream=true" \
  --output -
```

Eli K.: Notes: `-N` disables curl buffering so you can observe chunked data live; `-v` captures TLS handshake and headers. Ask them to save stdout and stderr to files: `curl ... > sse.out 2> sse.err` and attach both.

Maya (DevEx): Also request the debug bundle: include the curl verbose log (sse.err), server response headers (from `-D headers.txt`), and the original request id they logged in app. If they can, include proxy logs for the span around the trace.

Maria S.: Customer sent partial `sse.err` showing `* Received HTTP code 502 from proxy after CONNECT` and `* Empty reply from server`. They included `X-Trace: 7f9c2b1a` but no upstream req id.

Raj P.: Please ask them to rerun with this command to collect full trace and TLS ciphers: 

```
curl -v -N -w "\nEXIT_STATUS:%{exitcode}\nTIMINGS:time_namelookup=%{time_namelookup},time_connect=%{time_connect},time_starttransfer=%{time_starttransfer},time_total=%{time_total}\n" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: customer-req-7721" \
  -D headers.txt \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-xyz&stream=true" \
  > sse.out 2> sse.err
```

Raj P.: Ask them to ALSO run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -servername api.redwood.example -tlsextdebug` and attach the output if TLS renegotiation or proxy MITM is suspected.

Maya (DevEx): For our side, please collect the backend trace: `request-id` from headers (if present), proxy logs (nginx) around the timestamp, and the runtime logs for the serving node that handled `trace=7f9c2b1a`. I can map the trace to internal request ids if they give us the customer time and request id.

Maria S.: Customer says proxy timeouts after ~62s. Could be keepalive or proxy buffer config. Raj, can you check if we had any backend spikes at 2026-03-16T14:03Z?

Raj P.: I'll check infra metrics and the serving logs. Preliminary grep shows a short spike in p95 for tokenization at that minute but no full outage. I flagged the node handling that `trace=7f9c2b1a` — internal req id `rid-9b2e`. Will attach logs in thread when I have them.

infra-bot: Ticket #5821 created for customer (severity: high). Upload bundle instructions sent to customer email with pre-signed S3 link.

Eli K.: If we confirm proxy is cutting after 62s, workarounds: (1) suggest client use long keepalive and disable proxy buffering, (2) switch to chunk-based shorter heartbeats from server, or (3) route to Dedicated for that customer to eliminate intermediate proxies.

Maria S.: I'll push the repro command + the extra openssl step to the customer and request sse.out, sse.err, headers.txt, and any proxy logs. Will update with attachments. Thanks all.
